  note: IPv4: 4 cluster IP addresses of Kubernetes services were not examined. A cluster IP is no

  Fix first
    1. F1   INPUT accepts new connections to any port                                   +15, grade C
    2. F3   FORWARD accepts traffic that no rule names                                           +10
    3. F4   2 forwarded ports are open to any source                                              +4

  Findings

  HIGH     F1   INPUT accepts new connections to any port                                        -15
                No rule refuses them, and the policy of filter/INPUT is ACCEPT. Every port that no
                rule names is open: a service that listens on one, now or later, is reachable at
                once.
                fix  Add rules for the traffic that is needed and test them, with a way back, then
                     set the policy to DROP. The recommended baseline (--baseline) is a complete
                     rule set to start from.
                     Deny by default (IPv4):
                       iptables -P INPUT DROP

  HIGH     F2   4 services are open to any source because INPUT accepts by default               -14
                No rule names their ports: A service on 8472/udp; sshd on 22/tcp; kubelet on
                10250/tcp; kube-proxy on 10256/tcp. Close the default first; then accept each port
                that must stay reachable, for its clients only.

  HIGH     F3   FORWARD accepts traffic that no rule names                                       -10
                No rule refuses it, and the policy of filter/FORWARD is ACCEPT. The rules show that
                this host routes packets (address translation or Docker), so other hosts can send
                traffic through it to every network it reaches, including container and virtual
                networks.
                fix  Set the policy to DROP after the forwarding paths that are needed have rules.
                     Deny forwarding by default (IPv4):
                       iptables -P FORWARD DROP

  MEDIUM   F4   2 forwarded ports are open to any source                                          -4
                nat/PREROUTING translates these ports to another host, and filter/FORWARD accepts
                them from any source; the rules of filter/INPUT do not apply: IPv4 30080/tcp to
                10.244.0.10:8080, 10.244.0.11:8080; IPv4 30443/tcp to 10.244.0.12:8443.
                fix  kube-proxy writes this translation for a Service of type NodePort or
                     LoadBalancer, and it writes its chains again all the time. Limit the Service in
                     the cluster: set spec.loadBalancerSourceRanges, use a NetworkPolicy for the
                     pods, or use type ClusterIP when the port needs no clients outside the cluster.
                     To filter on the node, drop the port for other sources in the raw table, which
                     sees the packet before the translation. The command below is for port
                     30080/tcp. For each of the other ports (30443/tcp), run it again with its
                     protocol and its port.
                     Drop port 30080 for all but the known clients, in front of the translation:
                       iptables -t raw -I PREROUTING -m addrtype --dst-type LOCAL -p tcp -m tcp --dport 30080 ! -s <trusted-cidr> -j DROP

  LOW      F5   Forwarded port 80/tcp of 203.0.113.50 is open to any source                       -1
                nat/PREROUTING translates these ports to another host, and filter/FORWARD accepts
                them from any source; the rules of filter/INPUT do not apply: IPv4 80/tcp of
                203.0.113.50 to 10.244.0.10:8080, 10.244.0.11:8080.
                nat/KUBE-SEP-KTTG6H42UOAJUCVL #2:  -p tcp -m comment --comment "default/web" -m tcp -j DNAT --to-destination 10.244.0.10:8080
                  reached by PREROUTING #1 → KUBE-SERVICES #3 → KUBE-SVC-2CMXP7HKUVJN7L6M #2
                nat/KUBE-SEP-N4G2XR5TDX7PQE7P #2:  -p tcp -m comment --comment "default/web" -m tcp -j DNAT --to-destination 10.244.0.11:8080
                  reached by PREROUTING #1 → KUBE-SERVICES #3 → KUBE-SVC-2CMXP7HKUVJN7L6M #3
                fix  kube-proxy writes this translation for a Service of type NodePort or
                     LoadBalancer, and it writes its chains again all the time. Limit the Service in
                     the cluster: set spec.loadBalancerSourceRanges, use a NetworkPolicy for the
                     pods, or use type ClusterIP when the port needs no clients outside the cluster.
                     To filter on the node, drop the port for other sources in the raw table, which
                     sees the packet before the translation.
                     Drop port 80 for all but the known clients, in front of the translation:
                       iptables -t raw -I PREROUTING -d 203.0.113.50 -p tcp -m tcp --dport 80 ! -s <trusted-cidr> -j DROP
